newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain rate seen unchanged - Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain rate seen unchanged - Reuter poll.

text.p: The Bank of Spain is likely to keep its key money rate unchanged at 6.75 percent on Wednesday at its regular repo auction, a Reuter poll forecast.
All 10 financial analysts polled by Reuters on Tuesday ruled out a reduction, with many saying the central bank was now carefully watching inflation developments.
They said the Bank of Spain would likely wait to see if the October and November consumer price index (CPI) confirm further inflation drops before deciding on more cuts in official rates.
In September, CPI rose a less-than-expected 0.2 percent, following a 0.3-percent rise in August. Year-on-year inflation fell to 3.6 percent from 3.7 percent in August.
October CPI data are due on Thursday.
A Reuter poll forecast October CPI to rise 0.2 percent month-on-month and 3.6 percent year-on-year.

Analysts said the market was discounting an official rate cut by year-end of between 0.25 and 0.50 percent because they expected inflation to ease gradually to the three-percent level and then break that level by the first quarter of 1997.

On October 3, the Bank of Spain cut its official rate by 50 basis points to 6.75 percent, backing the government's austere 1997 budget package with its sixth official rate reduction this year. The rate started the year at nine percent.
